headline: Mistakes to Avoid After a Fire Incident
articleBody: It's tough when your home or business has been hit by fire, and in the chaos, it’s easy to make choices that could actually worsen the damage. One big mistake is delaying cleanup; corrosive ash and soot don't wait, and the longer they sit, the more permanent the damage becomes to surfaces and belongings. Another common pitfall is trying to clean soot yourself without the right gear or knowledge. Regular household cleaners usually just smear soot, embedding it deeper into materials and potentially spreading contaminants. Also, don't just air out your home with windows open, thinking it’ll fix the smoke smell. This can actually draw more soot particles into unaffected areas and won't eliminate embedded odors. And remember, turning on HVAC systems can spread soot and smoke particles throughout your property, creating a much larger problem. Finally, don't rush into repairs without a thorough assessment. What seems like minor damage might hide structural issues or pervasive smoke contamination. It’s always best to get a professional eye on it. Taking these precautions can really save you a lot of headache and extra costs down the line. When in doubt, call the pros at First To Respond Restoration for a clear path forward.
